title: Unreliable Narrator Framing as a Cost-effective Mechanism for Satire Explanation of Australian and American Satirical News
abstract: arXiv:2610.12863v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Satirical news is a unique form of misinformation: it is intended to be humorous by the original publication source but can be misinterpreted. Explanation of satirical news articles is challenging because recent and local context needs to be incorporated. This is a pilot study that explores explanation generation for satirical news articles from Australia and compares them alongside those from USA. The paper demonstrates that framing explanations on unreliable narrator theory on open-weights models can be a feasible, cost-effective alternative to frontier models. We find that models identify the satirical tropes more accurately on the American source than the Australian one. This work results in a novel dataset and an evaluation benchmark for satirical explanation.

translated_title: 不可靠叙述者框架作为解释澳大利亚与美国讽刺新闻的一种低成本机制
translated_abstract: 讽刺新闻是一种独特形式的错误信息：其原始发布来源本意是制造幽默，但可能被读者误解。对讽刺新闻文章进行解释具有挑战性，因为需要纳入最新的时事和本地背景信息。这是一项探索性研究，探讨为澳大利亚讽刺新闻文章生成解释，并将其与美国讽刺新闻进行对比。论文表明，在开放权重模型上基于不可靠叙述者理论构建解释框架，可以成为前沿模型的一种可行且低成本的替代方案。我们发现，模型对美国来源的讽刺套路的识别准确度高于澳大利亚来源。这项工作产出了一个新颖的数据集以及一个讽刺解释评估基准。
tldr: 该研究提出以不可靠叙述者理论为框架，利用开放权重模型低成本地为澳大利亚和美国讽刺新闻生成解释，并贡献了新的数据集与评估基准。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates that open-weights models framed around unreliable narrator theory provide a cost-effective alternative to frontier models for explaining Australian and American satirical news, contributing a novel dataset and evaluation benchmark.
